concerns.text: Task T049 introduces a 'data integrity validator' performing statistical sanity checks (distribution of log(rate), pKa ranges) not mandated by any FR or SC. FR-001 only requires filtering for missing/invalid data and normalization; adding statistical distribution validation is scope creep that relaxes the strict 'filter and exclude' constraint by introducing a new, unverified gate.

Task T042 mandates a strict 'FAIL LOUDLY' exit on network/API errors, contradicting FR-001's resilience requirement. FR-001 explicitly states the system must use a reaction-class-specific average Ea or flag/exclude records if data is missing, implying a resilient pipeline that continues processing valid records rather than halting entirely on transient fetch issues or partial data gaps.

Tasks T007a1-T007a4 mandate on-the-fly calculation of Hammett/Taft descriptors, directly contradicting the 'Assumptions' section in spec.md which states: 'The independent descriptor vector... does not require real-time calculation during the validation step.' This creates a semantic drift where the task enforces a computational method explicitly assumed unnecessary in the spec, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or contradict spec assumptions.

Task T048 implements a 'random baseline' generator by re-running the full SHAP pipeline on shuffled labels to create a null distribution. SC-003 and US-3 Acceptance Scenario 3 define the random baseline as 'shuffled labels' for the correlation test, implying a direct comparison of the metric on shuffled vs. real data. Re-running the expensive SHAP pipeline for every permutation is an unmandated complexity that risks violating FR-008 (time/memory constraints) and contradicts the simpler interpretation of the success criterion.

Task T047 implements a SIGALRM-based timeout with checkpoint saving. FR-008 and SC-005 only require enforcing a maximum time and triggering a 'graceful exit or sampling'. The spec does not mandate checkpoint saving or signal handlers; a hard kill (exit 137) or simple sampling is sufficient. This task introduces an unverified implementation detail (checkpointing) that may not be feasible within the 6-hour window, potentially weakening the 'graceful exit' constraint by adding failure points.
